ai.description: *Nanorana conaensis* is a small frog (SVL 30–35 mm) with a brown-mottled dorsal surface and yellowish belly. It is distinguished by its lack of a tympanum and presence of dense, dark throat speckling.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana conaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped spinules covering the entire dorsal surface and flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana conaensis* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations ranging from 3,500 to 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Cona Paa frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates near the high-altitude streams and rocky habitats of the Himalayas.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana conaensis* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs attached to submerged rocks or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana conaensis* is found in the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting alpine meadows at elevations between 3,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Cona Paa Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard near slow-moving streams or marshy habitats within its high-altitude range.
